I need to find two things in this codebase:

1. The function/method that actually executes outbound HTTP delivery of webhooks (notifications to external systems when content changes). Look for webhook delivery, sending, dispatching logic that makes the actual HTTP request.

2. The SSRF protection mechanism that prevents webhook URLs from targeting internal/private network addresses. Look for URL validation, IP filtering, private network checks, blocklists for internal addresses, etc.

Search breadth: very thorough. Look for terms like: webhook, deliver, dispatch, notify, outbound, SSRF, private, internal, allowlist, blocklist, reserved, loopback, filterUrl, validateUrl, isPrivate, isInternal, ssrf_filter, etc. Check across the entire codebase.

content.text:
I now have a complete picture. Here are my findings:

---

## 1. Webhook HTTP Delivery Function

The actual outbound HTTP delivery of webhooks is implemented in:

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**

The core function is `Post` (line 120), which:
- Marshals a `WebhookRequestPayload` to JSON (line 121)
- Creates an HTTP POST request targeting the webhook URL (line 126)
- Optionally computes an HMAC-SHA256 signature following the Standard Webhooks spec, setting `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers (lines 133-149)
- Executes the request via `safeClient.Do(req)` (line 152) -- the `safeClient` is an `http.Client` whose transport is wired to the SSRF-safe dialer (see below)
- Reads the response body (capped at 1 MB) and checks for a 2xx status code and a zero `code` in the JSON response body

There is also `PostAsync` (line 184), which enqueues the payload into a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128). Four goroutines are started at `init()` time (line 43) to drain the queue and call `Post` for each payload.

The dispatch layer that triggers delivery lives in:

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`**

This file provides four public methods on `APIV1Service`:
- `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (line 15)
- `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (line 20)
- `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (line 25)
- `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (line 30)

All route through the private `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` method (line 48), which looks up the user's configured webhooks via `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks`, builds a `WebhookRequestPayload`, and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)`.

These dispatchers are called from:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 157 (memo created), line 562 (memo deleted)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` line 67 (memo updated)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` line 119 (comment created)

---

## 2. SSRF Protection Mechanism

SSRF protection is implemented via a two-layer defense, both in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/`:

### Layer A: URL validation at webhook registration time

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`**, function `ValidateURL` (line 62):
- Parses the URL, requiring it to be an absolute URL with `http` or `https` scheme (rejecting `file://`, `gopher://`, etc.)
- Resolves the hostname via `net.LookupHost`
- Checks every resolved IP against `isReservedIP` (line 44), which compares the IP against a list of blocked CIDR ranges

This is called at webhook create and update time in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go` (lines 74, 161, 182).

### Layer B: Dial-time SSRF guard (defeats DNS rebinding)

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**, function `safeDialContext` (line 59):
- Replaces the default `net.Dialer.DialContext` in the HTTP transport used by `safeClient` (line 35)
- At connection time, re-resolves the hostname and checks every resolved IP against `isReservedIP` before allowing the TCP connection
- This is critical because it prevents DNS rebinding attacks where a hostname resolves to a public IP at validation time but a private IP at request time

### Blocked IP ranges

Defined in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go` lines 14-23 (`reservedCIDRs`):
- `127.0.0.0/8` -- IPv4 loopback
- `10.0.0.0/8` -- RFC-1918 class A private
- `172.16.0.0/12` -- RFC-1918 class B private
- `192.168.0.0/16` -- RFC-1918 class C private
- `169.254.0.0/16` -- Link-local (including cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254)
- `::1/128` -- IPv6 loopback
- `fc00::/7` -- IPv6 unique local
- `fe80::/10` -- IPv6 link-local

These are parsed into `[]*net.IPNet` at init time (line 28) and checked by `isReservedIP` (line 44).

### Escape hatch for self-hosted deployments

The package-level variable `AllowPrivateIPs` (line 41 of `validate.go`) can be set to `true` to disable the SSRF guard entirely. When true, `isReservedIP` always returns `false`. Currently, no production code sets this variable -- it is only toggled in tests (`webhook_test.go` lines 90-92, 141-143) to allow `httptest.NewServer` (which binds to 127.0.0.1) to work.
